title: Quarterly Dedicated Capacity sprint themes and experiment catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define the quarterly roadmap slice for Dedicated Capacity focused on predictable surge behavior, economics-aware autoscale policies, and a small catalog of tightly scoped experiments to de-risk production rollouts. This ticket consolidates sprint themes, acceptance criteria, runbook updates, and experiment definitions for Q2. Scope includes: surge window scheduling, fractional pool trials, prewarm/predictive heuristics, autoscale governance metrics and cost safeguards. Out of scope: major infra refactor or public pricing changes (will be separate PMs).
milestones: M1: Experiment catalog finalized and prioritized (by 2026-02-10)
M2: Two engineering spikes complete (kernel-level batching + predictive prewarm) (by 2026-02-24)
M3: Canary of fractional-pool allocation with rollback policy (by 2026-03-10)
M4: Runbook + console dashboard updates deployed, SLO/alert thresholds tuned (by 2026-03-20)
M5: Post-experiment economic analysis and decision: scale, iterate, or retire (by 2026-03-27)
acceptance_criteria: Experiment catalog contains at least three experiments with hypothesis, metric, rollout plan, and rollback criteria
Canary shows no >5% regression in tail latency for affected tenants during a 48h window
Cost delta for tested autoscale policy is measured and shows projected per-token saving/overhead
Runbook entries exist for surge window operations and automatic fallback triggers
Console surfaces new metrics (surge headroom, prewarm hit rate, fractional pool utilization)
risks: Predictive prewarm models produce false positives leading to cost spikes
Fractional pooling increases noisy-neighbor effects for latency-sensitive customers
Autoscale policy churn may conflict with existing SLA commitments for Dedicated customers
Insufficient observability into kernel-level batching makes regressions hard to diagnose
tradeoffs: Aggressive prewarm reduces cold-start latency but increases reserved GPU time (cost)
Tighter surge windows reduce cost but make burst capacity less available for unanticipated spikes
Fractional pools improve utilization but complicate billing attribution and troubleshooting
notes: We prioritize experiments that can be instrumented with minimal infra schema changes
Eng should avoid large refactors; prefer toggles and canary-first approach
Coordinate with Sales/CS for any customers in the canary cohort to set expectations
